subject.title: Discord account-to-agent routing falls back to default agent instead of matching by account name

question: Should Discord multi-account routing add a guarded same-name accountId-to-agent fallback when no explicit binding matches, or should explicit bindings remain the only supported routing contract?
rationale: The source-level gap is clear, but fallback behavior changes session, auth/provider, and security boundaries; root policy treats fallback behavior as a product decision rather than an implementation convenience.

options.title: Approve guarded fallback
options.body: Route non-default Discord accountIds to an existing same-named configured agent only after explicit binding tiers miss, with distinct diagnostics, docs, tests, and live Discord proof.

options.title: Keep explicit bindings only
options.body: Leave runtime behavior unchanged and add clearer docs or doctor/status warnings for Discord accounts that look intended to bind to same-named agents.

options.title: Repair the fork PR first
options.body: Use the open fork PR as source material only after resolving conflicts, adding the missing configured-agent guard, and supplying real Discord proof.

recommendation.title: Approve guarded fallback
recommendation.body: Route non-default Discord accountIds to an existing same-named configured agent only after explicit binding tiers miss, with distinct diagnostics, docs, tests, and live Discord proof.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest current and historical ownership signal across shared routing, Discord route resolution, and prior maintainer-facing analysis on this routing contract.
